articleTitle: Environmental impact of renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Environmental Impact of Renewable Energy Sources
abstract: Summary form only given. The CEGB have developed procedures for environmental assessment of large power stations. Preparation of an environmental statement is now a formal part of the consent application process. Some potential effects can be readily quantified, others are more subjective in nature. This is illustrated and issues relevant to renewable energy are discussed with particular reference to wind farms, where effects on landscape, noise, radio-communications and bird life are among the topics of interest.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Environmental studies in the Department of Energy's renewable energy programs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Environmental Impact of Renewable Energy Sources
abstract: All forms of energy production interact with the environment and this is particularly true for the renewable energy sources because the dilute energy content of the sources demands large-scale deployment of a technology to make an appreciable contribution to the UK's energy needs. Within the Department of Energy's renewable energy programme the constraints surrounding implementation of each of the technologies is being studies from two aspects: factors which limit exploitation of the resource in general (site availability); and site specific effects arising from the operation of a renewable energy plant. These aspects are inter-linked to some extent and do not relate equally to all the renewable sources. Examples of such studies for five renewable sources are discussed: refuse in landfill sites; short rotation energy forestry; wind energy; tidal barrages; and geothermal hot dry rocks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
